Tessa / Priyom — I ran a rapid model using the workbook Emily sent and Redwood benchmark kernels. High-level assumptions I used (documented in attached "redwood-sla-math-2025.pdf"):
- Model: rw-instruct-7b-quant (production profile)
- Effective generation rate per A100 80GB equiv (continuous batching, typical request length 200 tokens): ~3,600 tokens/sec
- End-to-end p95 target 300ms maps to per-request token budget of ~250 tokens for the generation portion in our measurements (includes decode time + small orchestrator overhead).

Sizing sketch (peak window):
- Peak QPS 18 RPS * median 900 tokens/session = 16,200 tokens/sec required (peak burst)
- 16,200 / 3,600 = 4.5 GPUs -> round up to 5 GPUs for nominal peak capacity

Headroom and operational considerations:
- We recommend 1.5x headroom for early-stage pilots (to cover sudden bursts and KV cache warming) -> 5 * 1.5 = 7.5 -> round up to 8 GPUs reserved.
- Quiet-hours effect: if peak is concentrated 18:00–23:00 and daytime is 1/5th of peak, autoscale/bursting rules can drop pool to 2 GPUs during day and scale up by pre-warming cache 30 minutes before evening peak.
- Latency sensitivity: if Brightline needs p95 <= 200ms, we model a need for faster variant (rw-instruct-7b-fp16) or double the GPUs because lower per-token throughput in lower-latency compiled path; call this out explicitly in the quote.

Operational notes:
- Memory posture: multi-turn context retention increases KV cache size; long histories (2k+ tokens) will reduce effective tokens/sec per GPU by ~10–15% in our runs; adjust headroom accordingly.
- Warm pools and scheduled pre-warm for predicted high-traffic days (Mon/Thu evening spikes) reduces cold-start p95 spikes.

I'll attach the PDFs and a quick GPU ramp schedule. If Emily can provide 90th percentile session tokens and whether they append full context each turn, we can tighten the numbers.

Michael / Emily — attached is a concise proposal based on the updated percentiles and multi-turn note (see attached PDF + workbook). TL;DR recommendation:

- Reserved baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (this covers sustained evenings with 1.5x headroom on median/90th traffic).
- Burst policy: +4 GPUs available via burst (elastic over-provision) for short windows (10–30 minutes) to contain 99th percentile journaling spikes.
- Autoscale rules: keep day pool at 2 GPUs, trigger pre-warm 30 min before expected evening peak; automated pre-warm adjusts for Monday/Sunday +25% expected uplift.
- Expected p95 under plan: ~260–320ms depending on session context length; 99th for long journaling sessions may hit ~800ms unless service uses streaming/partial response strategies.

Notes and next steps:
- If Brightline wants strict p95 <= 300ms at 99th percentile, recommended path is either: (a) larger reserved pool (12 GPUs) or (b) select lower-latency model variant and provision ~9 GPUs. We included both options in the attached cost/delivery sheet.
- We'll schedule a short ops-runbook review with your infra lead to confirm pre-warm triggers and alerting for cache pressure.
